sections.html:
Troup County sits on Georgia's western edge against the Alabama line. LaGrange is the county seat and largest city, and Hogansville and West Point are the other incorporated places. Long Cane, Mountville, Harrisonville and Abbottsford are unincorporated communities. Interstate 85 and Interstate 185 cross the county, so Atlanta commuters and Columbus-area workers both choose to live here.

A bungalow in LaGrange, a lakeside lot near West Point and a farm tract outside Hogansville attract quite different buyers, and each can come with its own tax history. Population is 72,844, which is 4.9% above the April 2020 base. Roughly 61 of every 100 housing units are lived in by their owners, and the middle owner-occupied value is $217,200. Seniors account for 17.8% of residents, so inherited houses and estate sales appear regularly.

Your tax passes through two separate desks. One collects money. The other, a citizens board served by the Property Appraisal Department, decides what the parcel is worth.

  • Tax commissioner: (706) 883-1620, open on weekdays from 8 to 5, for bills, mobile home and timber tax, and tag renewals.
  • Property Appraisal: (706) 883-1625, at 100 Ridley Avenue, Suite 2100, LaGrange, for values, returns, exemptions and appeals.
  • Superior Court clerk: where deeds and tax liens are recorded.

The assessors are a part-time citizens board, so a call may land on voicemail and be returned later. That board picks the Chief Appraiser and gets its budget from the county commission. Card and online payments run through the county portal, which has a Property Taxes choice, and the tax office also takes payment by phone.

sections.h2: Due dates and how the bill is figured
sections.html:
November 15 is the official deadline, with penalties and interest piling up after it. Counties may move the statewide default, so read the date printed on the bill you actually receive.

Georgia freezes market value as of January 1 and then taxes 40% of it. Millage comes from the school board, the county governing authority and any other body that covers your parcel. A sample calculation from the appraisal office uses .030260 as the rate and takes off exemptions first. Mobile homes and timber reach the same collector on their own timetables.

  • The state ratio is 40%, applied to market value.
  • One mill means a dollar per thousand dollars of assessed value.
  • A higher value or a dropped exemption can lift a bill while the rate stays flat.

Appeals grow out of the yearly assessment notice, and you get 45 days after the notice date shown on its face. Once that passes, you lose the chance to challenge that year's number.

The appraisers want sales records, photos of similar houses that changed hands lately, and whatever else supports your figure. A Board of Equalization hearing usually follows. Grand jurors name its members, who are neighbors and fellow owners, and filing is free. Arbitration is the other lane: each party hires one arbitrator and splits a third. Going on to Superior Court adds a $25.00 filing fee.

After a board or court rules, the assessors cannot move that value for two years without walking the parcel themselves.

sections.h2: City bills in LaGrange, Hogansville and West Point
sections.html:
Possibly. A city levies its own ad valorem tax, and its clerk bills and collects it, unless the city and county have agreed to one combined statement. Ask the tax commissioner at (706) 883-1620 and the clerk of your city before you assume one payoff covers everything.

Taxpayers get at least 60 days from the postmark of a bill before interest starts. A parcel inside city limits can therefore owe two separate payoffs at closing, one to the county and one to City Hall, and each may carry its own due date. Collect both figures in writing.

Homestead filings are taken from the first of January through April 1. Miss the window and you forfeit the benefit for that year. Property Appraisal at (706) 883-1625 hands out the forms and quotes the amounts.

Other special exemptions are kept in the same office. Skipping a return means you are deemed to have returned the same property at last year's final value, and freeport relief for inventory needs a local vote. A move means filing again for the new address.

  • Own the house and live in it on January 1.
  • A refund claim for a tax wrongly assessed has a three-year limit from payment.
  • Mobile homes sit on a separate location permit and return cycle.

Troup County has several moving parts, so work through them in order and keep every figure in writing.

  1. Call the tax commissioner at (706) 883-1620 and ask for the balance on each year still open, including any mobile home or timber account.
  2. If the house is inside LaGrange, Hogansville or West Point, ask the city clerk for a separate payoff.
  3. Call Property Appraisal at (706) 883-1625 to confirm your homestead is on file and to ask whether a recent change to the house has been picked up.
  4. Ask the Superior Court clerk whether any lien is recorded against the parcel.
  5. Give the payoff letters to the attorney or title agent handling the sale.

Written figures matter because interest and penalties keep building, and a verbal quote from last month may fall short. The payoffs come out of your proceeds, so you will know your net before you commit to a price. Sellers of inherited or estate-held or long-vacant houses should allow extra time, since several years of records may need to be pulled.

Ask the collector for a payoff amount ahead of scheduling the closing, and let the attorney or title agent pay it from what you receive. Each year's bill goes to whoever held title on January 1, so an October sale can still leave a statement in your mailbox unless the settlement sheet divides the tax.

The tax commissioner's news page posts a courtesy tax sale list. Excess funds after such a sale go only to the record owner at that time or to other lienholders. A home that spent years as a rental, an estate asset or an empty shell may owe for several years, so request every year's status in writing.

A cash buyer can still close while a balance is open, because the payoff is deducted at the table. Set the closing statement next to the payoff letter and compare each line. Bring your parcel number and a copy of your deed when you call or visit, and ask the clerk of superior court whether any lien is recorded against the property.

faqs.q: How do I phone the Troup County tax office?
faqs.a: The number is (706) 883-1620. Questions about value or exemptions go to Property Appraisal at (706) 883-1625.

faqs.q: Is November 15 the Troup County payment deadline?
faqs.a: Yes. November 15 is the official deadline, and penalties and interest follow it. Confirm against your own statement.

faqs.q: How long can I challenge a Troup County assessment?
faqs.a: Forty-five days after the notice date. A late filing forfeits the right for that year, and appeals cannot be filed without a notice.

faqs.q: When does Troup County take homestead applications?
faqs.a: From New Year's Day through April 1. Anything filed later waits for the next year.

faqs.q: Who owes the tax if I sell in October?
faqs.a: The person who owned it on January 1 is billed. Pay it at closing, after getting the payoff letter from the tax commissioner.
